problem:
$$
{A}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,{A}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Find the matrix $C$ given that $B={{A}_{1},{A}_{2}}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{A}_{1},{A}_{2}},$ and the coordinates of the matrix $C$ relative to $B$ are $[C]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

activity_context.topic_title: The Coordinates of a Vector Relative to a Basis in Abstract Vector Spaces

feedback.problem:
Consider the polynomials ${p}_{1}(t)$ and ${p}_{2}(t),$ given by

$$
{p}_{1}(t)=1-t+2{t}^{2},\,{p}_{2}(t)=t-{t}^{2}.
$$

Find $p(t)$ given that $B={{p}_{1}(t),{p}_{2}(t)}$ is a basis of $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}},$ and the coordinates of $p(t)$ relative to $B$ are $[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Any vector in  $\text{Span}{{p}_{1},{p}_{2}}$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{p}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}{p}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
[p(t)]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}p(t) & =1\cdot (1-t+2{t}^{2})+3\cdot (t-{t}^{2}) \\  & =1-t+2{t}^{2}+3t-3{t}^{2} \\  & =1+2t-{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
